Ether’s Field

Feel your music as living light.

A sound-reactive visualizer for musicians, meditators and visual artists. Sand settles into cymatic figures, flames dance to the kick drum, and a live solar system lines the planets up on any date from 1800 to 2050.

  • Stellar Alignment: real NASA orbits, planet meanings and sky reports
  • Cymatic plates in sand, fire, water, air and ether
  • Chakra colours and tones from 396 to 963 Hz
  • Beat detection and a guided breath pace
  • Records video with sound, straight from the screen
  • Installs on a phone and works offline

Ether Beat Lab

Press randomize, find a groove, shape it by hand.

A beat maker where every sound is synthesized in the browser. Nine genres, 53 instruments and a twelve-track sequencer, with WAV and timing-marker exports that drop straight into Ether Cut.

  • Boom Bap, Lo-fi, Trap, Drill, House, Afrobeats and more
  • One-press randomize, with locks for what you keep
  • Ether Voices, Atmos and World instruments
  • Sixteen pads and an MPC-style sampler
  • World scales such as Hijaz, Bhairav and Pelog
  • Exports WAV and beat markers for Ether Cut

Ether Cut

Cut a music video to the beat, in the browser.

Drop in videos, images and a song, arrange them on a timeline or storyboard, time the scenes to the music and export a finished video. Nothing is uploaded.

  • Timeline and storyboard, in 21:9, 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1
  • Tap to mark scenes on the beat
  • Keyframes, layers and blend modes
  • GPU looks: glow, light leak, grain, glitch, kaleidoscope
  • Particles, beat-reactive pulses and animated text
  • Exports MP4 or WebM

Ether Image Studio

146 looks from around the world. Blend up to four.

Choose image styles, 3D looks, Japanese anime, donghua, world styles and Ether Visions, then set the scene, characters, location, light and film look. The studio writes a still-image prompt and a matching motion prompt to animate it.

  • Blend 2, 3 or 4 looks, or let it surprise you
  • 570 locations in 12 categories
  • A saved cast of characters with reference sheets
  • 33 anime looks by era, genre and approach
  • Image and motion prompts, ready to copy
  • Everything saved in your browser, with backup

Ether’s View

From the Big Bang to the farthest known worlds.

An interactive journey through the universe. It opens on the Big Bang, set to Ether’s song Zero Point Genesis, then lets you roam: planets on their real orbits, moons, dwarf planets, double-sun systems, nebulae, black holes and the Milky Way.

  • The Big Bang as a particle simulation, timed to the song
  • Real Sun, Moon and planet positions for any date
  • Today’s Planetary Alchemy: a daily reading of the sky
  • Double-sun worlds such as Kepler-16 and Kepler-47
  • Time travel from the Big Bang to 100 trillion years ahead
  • Quantum strings: a music-reactive web of light

Ether’s Celestial Atlas

All 88 constellations, on a sky you can turn.

A star atlas with the 88 IAU constellations and 5,044 background stars. Pick a constellation to light up its pattern and read the names of its stars, with its astronomy beside Nirayana correspondences and symbolic reflections.

  • Search all 88, or filter by hemisphere or the 12 rashis
  • 757 pattern stars with their names and designations
  • Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom
  • Lines, names and the coordinate grid on or off
  • Astronomy, Nirayana and symbolism for each one
  • One file: nothing to install, no server

Ether Explains

3D animated explainers, built with Claude.

Pick a look, write the story and copy the prompt into Claude. Paste back the three.js scene it writes, play it, ask for changes, then record it with your voiceover as a video. No accounts and no API keys.

  • 37 looks, from Low-Poly to Glass and Light
  • 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1
  • A voiceover SRT lands each beat on its line
  • Revisions carry player errors back to Claude
  • Every version kept; projects export as .json
  • Records MP4 or WebM with your voice

Ether Voice Reader

Let the words find their voice.

A quiet reading space for passages and plain-text files. The Mac app narrates in your own voice, generated on your Mac with no cloud voice service. The browser version reads aloud, keeps bookmarks and listens for spoken commands.

  • A mic test with a live meter and level advice
  • Lossless voice recording on the Mac
  • Narration in your voice, saved as WAV
  • Voice Studio in the browser: record and clean up a sample
  • Spoken controls such as “reader play” and “reader next”
  • Your text and bookmarks stay on your device
Open in the browserView the code
Mac app · open sourceSwift · Blender · local AI

Ethers Prism

Don’t ask the AI for the thing. Ask it for an instrument to make the thing.

Describe a goal and Ethers Prism builds you an editor: dials with named ends, plus fixed requirements. Move the dials, sweep one across its range, branch through history, and render the version you choose with an authorship log. It all runs on your Mac.

  • Eight fields, from Text and Image to Beats
  • 3D Stage, Animation and Line Logo in Blender
  • Agents on Claude, LM Studio or Ollama
  • Teach by example from your starred results
  • Beats built from your own sample library
  • A Checker that flags problems and never rewrites

About Ether

Ether is a state of mind, and the expression of whatever medium carries the art.

Ether makes AI art and music in many voices, writes books drawn from lived experience, and animates the characters of Zero’s Journey, where Ether travels with Element, a tiger who changes form with each world.

The apps here grew out of that work. They are the tools Ether wanted for making music videos, finding visual styles, sitting quietly with sound and light, exploring the sky, explaining ideas in 3D and hearing words read in a voice of one’s own.
